title: Generation of Gaussian 09 Input Files for the Computation of <sup>1</sup>H and <sup>13</sup>C NMR Chemical Shifts of Structures from a Spartan’14 Conformational Search
protocol: Draw cis-3-methylcyclohexanol in the Spartan workspace.
Select File → New to open the Model Kit toolbar.
Change the Rings drop down menu to Cyclohexane and click inside the workspace to add a parent cyclohexane molecule.
Select the Csp3 button within the Model Kit toolbar and click one of the yellow open valences on the cyclohexane ring.
Select the Osp3 button within the Model Kit toolbar and click a yellow open valence on the cyclohexane ring that is both two carbons separated from and cis to the previously added methyl group.
Ensure that the overall structure is cis-3-methylcyclohexanol before continuing.
Cleanup the preliminary geometry by clicking the Minimize button or selecting Build → Minimize.
Select Setup → Calculations.
Change the Calculate: drop down menu selection to Conformer Distribution.
Change the two drop down menus to Molecular Mechanics and MMFF.
Check the box next to Maximum: and change the conformers examined to “1000”.
Click Submit and save computational file as “cis-3-methylcyclohexanol” in a convenient directory.
Click OK indicating that the conformational search has started.
Select File → Close when job completion window appears.
Open the conformational search output file “cis-3-methylcyclohexanol.spartan.”
Ensure all expected conformers have been found by the calculation.
Select Display → Spreadsheet to view structures found during the conformational search.
Export the library of conformers as a single “.sdf” file.
Select File → Save As… to open a Save As window.
Enter “cis-3-methylcyclohexanol” as the filename.
Change the Save as type: drop down menu selection to MDL SD (*.sdf).
Click Save.
If a popup window appears with the title Select molecules, click Write all molecules followed by OK.
Click OK in the popup window that confirms the file export.
Download the "write-g09-inputs-sdf.py" script from Supplementary Data 1 to the directory containing the ".sdf" file created in Step 7.
If using Python version 2, download the "write-g09-inputs-sdf.py" script located in the Python-Version-2 directory within Supplementary Data 1.
Ensure the downloaded Python script is compatible with both the Python and Gaussian versions to be used.
Edit the “write-g09-inputs-sdf.py” Python script to change the memory and number of processors used in Gaussian calculations.
Open the “write-g09-inputs-sdf.py” Python script in IDLE or any other Python script editor.
Adjust the amount of memory for Gaussian 09 optimization/frequency jobs by changing the number to the right of “%mem=” on line 86.
Adjust the number of core processors for Gaussian 09 optimization/frequency jobs by changing the number to the right of “%nproc=” on line 87.
Adjust the amount of memory for Gaussian 09 NMR jobs by changing the number to the right of “%mem=” on line 113.
Adjust the number of core processors for Gaussian 09 NMR jobs by changing the number to the right of “%nproc=” on line 114.
Save the edited script file in the same directory as the “.sdf” file.
Navigate to the directory containing the “.sdf” file, the “write-g09-inputs-sdf.py” Python script, and associated computational files using a command line interface application.
Execute the “write-g09-inputs-sdf.py” Python script by entering the following command: python write-g09-inputs-sdf.py cis-3-methylcyclohexanol.sdf
Enter the name of the candidate structure as "cis-3-methylcyclohexanol".
Execute the script to create Gaussian input files for each unique structure within the cis-3-methylcyclohexanol.sdf file.
Move all created Gaussian input files into a new directory labeled "cis-3-methylcyclohexanol-gaussian_files".
Perform DFT calculations using Gaussian 09.
Obtain NMR data for the candidate structure from Step 12 input files.
Calculate DFT-optimized conformer geometries.
Compute free energies using “opt_freq-conf” input files.
Determine NMR shielding tensors using “nmr-conf” input files.
Assemble free energy and NMR shielding tensor data into spreadsheet files.
Reference and scale the NMR data.
Determine Boltzmann weighting factors for all conformers.
Apply weighting factors to generate Boltzmann-weighted chemical shifts.
